title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Smoked haddock, rice, boiled eggs, and curry spices
excerpt: The quintessential British breakfast dish, flaked smoked haddock with basmati rice, soft-boiled eggs, and a gentle curry spicing. A direct descendant of the Indian kitchuri brought back by returning colonists in the nineteenth century.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree descends from the Indian dish khichdi, a simple preparation of rice and lentils eaten across the subcontinent. British colonists encountered it and adapted it heavily on return, adding smoked fish and hard-boiled eggs and introducing the spiced cream version. By the Victorian era kedgeree was a standard British breakfast-table dish, particularly in country houses. The name itself is an anglicisation of khichdi.

recipeTools.notes: Wide pan for finishing the rice and fish.

content.text: Use naturally smoked haddock where you can, the dyed yellow fillets are fine in flavour but the colouring leaches into the milk during poaching. The eggs should be just-set in the yolk: lower into boiling water for exactly 7 minutes then cool in cold water. Cook the rice ahead if you are making this for breakfast. Cold rice fried briefly in the butter picks up a better texture than freshly cooked.

Place the haddock in a wide pan with the milk and bay leaves. Bring to a very gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish just flakes. Remove the fish, cool slightly, then flake into large pieces discarding the skin and bones. Reserve 100 ml of the poaching milk.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions until just tender. Drain and spread on a tray to cool and dry slightly.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, then transfer to cold water. Peel and halve.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 10 minutes until golden. Add the cumin seeds and cook for 1 minute. Add the ground spices and stir for 1 minute. Add the rice and toss to coat in the spiced butter.

Pour in the cream and reserved poaching milk. Fold in the flaked haddock gently so it does not break down further. Warm through over low heat, 3 to 4 minutes. Season carefully, the fish is salty. Divide into bowls, top with the egg halves and parsley, and serve with lemon wedges.
